growth_signal.value: Valuation reportedly doubled in under a year: it reached unicorn status at $1.5B with a $250M round, then raised $300M more.

entry.idea: Companies running apps in the cloud struggle to spot and stop security problems while they are actually happening, so Upwind built a platform that watches cloud workloads in real time and reacts to threats as they occur.
entry.lesson: In a hot, well-funded category, keep raising money and buying smaller rivals to stay ahead of fast-moving competitors.
entry.name: Upwind

growth.reason: Its valuation reportedly doubled in under a year through back-to-back funding rounds.

market.reason: Almost every company running workloads in the cloud needs security tools like this, a very large worldwide market.

tech.reason: Its real-time cloud security approach is strong enough to win huge rounds at a fast-rising valuation, though rivals in cloud security could catch up within a year or two.

entry.twist: It just bought an Israeli AI security startup, Aegis, and opened a new cyber research lab to add AI-driven detection on top of its existing runtime protection.
entry.who_pays: Companies that run their applications in the cloud pay for ongoing security monitoring and protection.
entry.why_now: More companies are moving fast-changing workloads to the cloud, and investors are pouring huge rounds into cloud-security startups right now.
